speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: asked the Minister for National Development whether more details can be provided regarding the usage of CPF funds for buying HDB flats with remaining leases of less than 60 years.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: asked the Minister for National Development in view of the increasing number of elderly Singaporeans with HDB flats and private properties with leases of less than 60 years and the restrictions on the use of CPF for such properties, what measures are in place to assist such owners who have difficulty selling their properties to downgrade to smaller flats or properties.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Potential buyers of such properties come from a wide spectrum of life stages and circumstances and have different housing needs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, elderly buyers, or families who are not yet ready to commit to a longer lease, may choose to buy a residential property with a shorter lease.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Older residential properties are also attractive to some buyers as they are usually more centrally located and served by established amenities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Government will continue to monitor the market and review the policies to help Singaporeans with their housing monetisation options.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The last time I looked at it, for a person who is 21 years old, to buy a flat of 60 years left, he can only finance 40%-odd of the lease.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Would the Minister consider putting in a higher percentage or can the Minister do something to help the "financiability" of older flats?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As I mentioned, there is a series of CPF rules today pertaining to the purchase of shorter lease flats.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But we will be able to share when we are ready with our review.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Can I clarify with the Minister if there are any plans to review the attractiveness of the Lease Buyback Scheme in view of the relatively low take-up to date?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Inherently, the amount that you can unlock from the Lease Buyback Scheme, particularly for larger flats, may be smaller than the amount that you can get if you were to sell the flat in the resale market and right size.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is understandable because if you sell the entire flat, you get larger proceeds; but with Lease Buyback Scheme, you are selling only part of the lease.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There will be differences in the proceeds that a senior can get from right-sizing versus Lease Buyback.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The point is that we are trying to make available more options so that seniors can decide, one way or the other, whatever their circumstances are.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think that is the basis for our thinking around these schemes, and, as I have mentioned earlier, we will continue to review them and make sure that Singaporeans in HDB flats will have a range of options to unlock the value of their flats for retirement.
